review_type: post-hoc target-metadata correction and response re-adjudication

corrected_target.summary: Unrestricted schema/resource download enables blind SSRF; large downloads can cause denial of service
corrected_target.original_metadata_fix_commit_disposition: b46cb1f fixes issue #1169, a DTD SYSTEM identifier/XML validation behavior bug; it is not the CVE-2022-0671 security remediation.

evidence.detail: case-039 source is commit 4a1b5298335fb7bfa1837052ec0e8e08933de6e1, recorded as 0.18.5-SNAPSHOT, dated 2022-02-08; it predates PR #1174, merged 2022-02-14.
Describes schema download leading to blind SSRF or DoS via a large file, and identifies versions before 0.19.0 as affected.
Merged on 2022-02-14; changes CacheResourcesManager resource downloads to restrict protocols and reject insecure redirects. The PR is included in the 0.19.0 release.
The commit title and linked issue #1169 concern DTD SYSTEM identifiers breaking XML validation, not the schema-download SSRF/DoS fix.

candidate_adjudication.rubric: The designated target is hit when the one candidate identifies the schema/resource-fetch path and the CVE's SSRF impact in vulnerable source. Merely sharing CWE-918 or mentioning XML is insufficient.

B0_original.reason: The original response did not satisfy the required response format.

B0_format_retry.reason: The candidate traces attacker-controlled XSD/DTD SYSTEM references through LemMinX's resource resolver and identifies outbound requests to attacker-chosen hosts, including SSRF. The retry is used only in the separately labelled format-corrected analysis.

P1_original.reason: The candidate identifies attacker-controlled schema/DTD SYSTEM references and outbound requests through the URI resolver to attacker-chosen/internal destinations, matching the SSRF component of CVE-2022-0671.

limits: Neither response was dynamically reproduced in this adjudication.
The candidates emphasize external-entity processing and entity-expansion risk; they do not independently establish the large-download DoS aspect or every protocol/redirect detail of the patch.
This target-metadata repair was performed after model outputs were reviewed and is therefore a post-hoc correction, not a preregistered judgment.
